headline: Documentation and code repos not discovered; protocol website and GitHub context missing.

findings.text: Block-explorer name-tag searches for 'edgeX Bridge' on Ethereum, edgeX L1, Arbitrum, and Binance block explorers did not surface protocol-specific contract labels. Search results included other bridge-related contracts and EdgeX Foundry (IoT platform) false positives.

Protocol website (https://pro.edgex.exchange/referral/196451583) fetched but returned only minimal meta-description without a link to a 'Deployed contracts' or 'Addresses' documentation page. No deployment registry URL identified.
No audit links were recorded in the per-protocol context (protocol.audit_links empty). No PDFs were fetched or reviewed for in-scope contract addresses.
No GitHub repository URL was recorded in the per-protocol context (protocol.github null). No Foundry broadcast artifacts, hardhat-deploy manifests, or manual address indexes could be inspected.
Protocol spans Ethereum, edgeX L1, Arbitrum, and Binance chains. No per-chain block-explorer results yielded contract addresses with protocol branding.
No factory contracts were surfaced from D1–D4, so factory-child enumeration was not performed.
No addresses catalogued; role taxonomy not applied.
No addresses in admin_addresses array; integrity check not applicable.

rationale.verdict: Unable to catalogue bridge contracts due to missing pinned GitHub repository, missing audit links, and unavailable deployed-contracts documentation. Website fetch returned minimal metadata. Block-explorer searches returned no protocol-specific tagged addresses. Off-chain documentation (edgeX Docs GitBook) describes edgeX as a perpetuals execution layer, not explicitly as a bridge; bridge-specific contract addresses were not located in accessible documentation.

evidence.shows: Protocol website returns minimal HTML metadata; no links to deployment addresses or bridge contract registry page.

Official edgeX documentation describes EDGE Stack as an app-specific execution layer for perpetuals with modular multi-VM architecture (edgeVM for perpetuals, edgeEVM for DeFi logic), deployed on Ethereum as a rollup. Does not explicitly document a standalone bridge component or bridge contract addresses.

unknowns: D1: Etherscan name-tag search for 'edgeX Bridge' returned bridge-related generic contracts (Hop Protocol, HASHI Bridge, SORA Bridge) but no edgeX-labeled addresses.

D1-offchain: Block-explorer searches require direct URL enumeration or dedicated API access not available in this run; recommend re-attempting with site-scoped search operators or manual Etherscan/Arbiscan/Binance name-tag crawl.
D2: No canonical 'Deployed Contracts' documentation page located. Website fetch did not include navigation to docs subdomain or deployment registry.
D4: GitHub repository URL not pinned in per-protocol context; cannot inspect broadcast/ or deployments/ artifacts.
D3: No audit links pinned; no in-scope contract addresses extracted from audit PDFs.
D5: edgeX L1 (non-standard EVM chain) has limited block-explorer availability; no canonical explorer URL assumed for this chain.

protocol_metadata.about: edgeX is building a parallel, modular execution app-specific execution layer optimized for high-performance on-chain trading. The EDGE Stack uses a modular multi-VM architecture with edgeVM for perpetual execution and edgeEVM for standard DeFi logic, deployed as a rollup on Ethereum. The protocol is incubated by Amber Group and has received strategic investment from Circle Ventures. No dedicated bridge component documentation was located.
